schema: id, app, surface, window_title, page_title, typed_text, sent (true=send detected by code, false=known not sent, null=unknown), following_actions, expected_lines (acceptable targets; wording may differ, lead word and recipient must match), must_not (regexes the output must not match), plus seal, to, in, writer, notes

fixtures.typed_text: Okay, you can go ahead and turn on the weekly report emails for the team. Secondly, I know that I mentioned making the dashboard faster. To really make it fast and to make the charts show up before the tables load, etc. For instance, ask claude to make dashboard charts render much faster could be a good note for this. Does that make sense to you? Lets brainstorm how it loads now and how you think it could load faster. Thank you! Also for the pricing page it should be plans side by side with the signup button under each plan and the FAQ below. Right now they are stacked on top of each other. Make sure on a small laptop screen the person would be able to see all three plans without scrolling down. Let me know if there is anything else as well
expected_lines: Approved the weekly report emails for the team.
Asked Claude to make the dashboard charts load before the tables.
Asked Claude to put the pricing plans side by side with a signup button under each.
Asked Claude to keep all three plans visible on a small laptop screen.
must_not: (?i)ask claude to make dashboard charts render much faster
fixtures.notes: Made-up message 1 (same shape as a real long request), typed in one go then Return. 750 chars: needs the 1,600-char view (only 240 reach the local writer). Approved is allowed by the cue 'go ahead'. At most 3 lines per send: the pricing layout lines may share a bullet. Its own wording copies 7 words in a row and must be refused by the copy rule.
